title: Cross-SDK: Graceful stream reconnects, TCP socket reuse, and transport presets
creator: Maya Chen
description: Unify pragmatic cross-language transport defaults and add ergonomic streaming reconnects. This ticket defines recommended defaults and implements SDK changes (Python, TypeScript, Go) for: (1) per-request and overall deadlines, (2) connection pool sizing and idle/keepalive tuning, (3) TCP socket reuse and socket-level keepalive configuration where platform allows, and (4) streaming client ergonomics and automatic graceful reconnect/backfill for transient network failures. Goal: reduce SLO violations for transient network/errors while keeping host-level concurrent connection counts bounded and preserving low tail-latency for short requests.
acceptance_criteria: SDKs expose a single, documented transport presets API that sets safe defaults for connect_timeout, request_deadline, max_connections_per_host, and idle_socket_ttl
Default presets implemented for Python (httpx/requests adapter), TypeScript (fetch/node http agent), and Go (http.Client + custom Transport) with consistent semantic behavior

Streaming client APIs gain a small reconnect/backoff strategy: transparent reconnect with resume where backend supports partial stream replay (or automatic client-side re-request with prefix-kv cache), and documented behavior when resume is not possible
E2E test harness simulating transient TCP resets validates reconnection/backfill behavior for each SDK
Telemetry events emitted for connect_timeout, pool_exhaustion, stream_reconnect, and stream_resume_failures (so we can correlate to SLOs)
Rollout plan included: minor version release for each SDK, feature flag to enable aggressive socket reuse, and canary to 10% of traffic for one week
comments: 2025-09-03 Maya Chen: Initial RFC drafted. Focus areas: timeouts that are easy to reason about for app developers (connect, first-byte/stream, overall request deadline) + pool defaults tuned to typical Redwood workloads (many short generation requests + occasional long streaming).

2025-09-04 Samir Patel: Proposed defaults in RFC: connect_timeout=500ms, first_byte_timeout=1s, overall_deadline=60s, max_connections_per_host=12 (node/ts), 24 (python), idle_socket_ttl=90s. I tested locally against loadgen — reduced connection churn vs naive defaults.

2025-09-05 Ana Reyes (Design): UX note — expose presets as Transport.Presets.LOW_LATENCY, BALANCED, HIGH_THROUGHPUT. SDKs should provide small helper factory functions to construct clients with these presets.

2025-09-06 Noah Li (Go): Implemented custom Transport wrapper for Go that enables TCP keepalive probe configuration and socket reuse. Added unit tests around dialer timeouts and idle connection cleanup.

2025-09-08 Maya Chen: Added streaming reconnect design: client will attempt up to 3 reconnects with exponential backoff (100ms, 300ms, 900ms) if socket drops during active stream. If the server supports resume tokens or prefix KV cache, client will request resume; otherwise it will re-issue the request and rely on application-level dedup/resume. Documented semantic differences per runtime.

2025-09-09 Samir Patel: Opened PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/pull/1786, https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/2045, https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-go/pull/712. CI flaky test observed in TS streaming tests (race on event emitter) — investigating.

2025-09-11 Maya Chen: Added telemetry mapping: events.stream_reconnect, events.stream_resume_attempt, metrics.pool_wait_time_ms. Coordinate with observability team to add dashboard panels for these metrics.
2025-09-12 Samir Patel: Integration loadtest scheduled on staging for 2025-09-15 with 50k short requests and 1k concurrent streams. Canary plan drafted in Releases doc.
